Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The country's exports recorded a 16.6% increase in April-September this fiscal and India is on track to hit the $1 trillion exports target in 2026-27, Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal said on Wednesday (November 18, 2026). Talking in a session organised by the industry chamber FICCI, the Secretary said despite global uncertainties on the trade front, India is doing well. "We are on track to hit $1 trillion exports [of goods and services] this year," Mr. Agrawal said. Last fiscal, India had touched an all-time high of $863 billion. He said that in uncertain times, India has an advantage as a "trusted" trading partner.

"We are on track to hit $1 trillion exports [of goods and services] this year," Mr. Agrawal said. Last fiscal, India had touched an all-time high of $863 billion. articles.title: UN Sustainable Development Goals group for science, technology rejigged
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The group has been constituted even as the international community ramps up efforts to achieve the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres has reconstituted a 10-member group that works on promoting science, technology and innovation toward achieving its Sustainable Development Goals. The lone Indian in this group is former biologist and former Council of Scientific and Industrial Research CSIR Director General, Shekhar Mande, who is also currently President, Indian National Science Academy. The group has been constituted even as the international community ramps up efforts to achieve the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, while preparing for the 2027 SDG Summit. “The group comprises distinguished experts from diverse geographic and disciplinary backgrounds from both developing and developed countries. Each member, recognised for their international excellence in science or technology, brings a wealth of experience and insight from civil society, the private sector, and the scientific community, underscoring the inclusive and comprehensive approach the UN is taking towards sustainable development,” an accompanying press statement noted. The other members of the group are Marian Dorcas Quain (Ghana), Deputy Director-General of CSIR Ghana; Giorgio Rossi (Italy), Vice-President of Elettra-Sincrotrone Trieste; Magnus Andersson (Sweden), Associate Professor at Malmö University; Mônica Tejo Cavalcanti (Brazil), Professor at the Federal University of Campina Grande; Evgeniya Dmitrieva (Russia), Member of the Civic Chamber of the Russian Federation; Motoko Kotani (Japan), Executive Director of Science at RIKEN; Jin Li (China), President of Fudan University; Madin Maseeh (Maldives), President of the Maldives Space Research Organisation; and Rita Orji (Nigeria), Canada Research Chair in Persuasive Technology at Dalhousie University. Professor Mande is also President of Vijnana Bharti, which, along with the Ministry of Science and Technology is gearing up to host the India International Science Festival in Pune in December. Announcing this on Wednesday (November 18, 2026), Union Minister of Science Jitendra Singh said at a press briefing that the government had taken a conscious decision to replace “scattered, repetitive gatherings”, including the erstwhile Indian Science Congress, with two flagship national events carrying distinct identities.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: While the Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave in October saw 13 Ministries and Nobel Laureates, and was an academic-driven conclave exploring frontier themes, the India International Science Festival (IISF) brought a “festive, public-facing character with international resonance”. By rotating the venue to different regions, after Chandigarh, Hyderabad, Goa and Delhi, bringing IISF for the first time to Pune leverages the western hub’s vibrant academic, research, and industrial ecosystem.

hinglishTracks.en: The United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres has reconstituted a 10-member group that works on promoting science, technology and innovation toward achieving its Sustainable Development Goals.

hinglishTracks.en: Professor Mande is also President of Vijnana Bharti, which, along with the Ministry of Science and Technology is gearing up to host the India International Science Festival in Pune in December.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — प्रोफेसर मांडे विज्ञान भारती के अध्यक्ष भी हैं, जो विज्ञान और प्रौद्योगिकी मंत्रालय के साथ मिलकर दिसंबर में पुणे में भारत अंतर्राष्ट्रीय विज्ञान महोत्सव की मेजबानी करने की तैयारी कर रहा है।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'International' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'International' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive और Antonyms हैं: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile।

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #21 of 30 (18 NOV)

📰 UN Sustainable Development Goals group for science, technology rejigged

📌 Published: 18 Nov 2026, 11:15:54 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The group has been constituted even as the international community ramps up efforts to achieve the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres has reconstituted a 10-member group that works on promoting science, technology and innovation toward achieving its Sustainable Development Goals. The lone Indian in this group is former biologist and former Council of Scientific and Industrial Research CSIR Director General, Shekhar Mande, who is also currently President, Indian National Science Academy. The group has been constituted even as the international community ramps up efforts to achieve the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, while preparing for the 2027 SDG Summit. “The group comprises distinguished experts from diverse geographic and disciplinary backgrounds from both developing and developed countries. Each member, recognised for their international excellence in science or technology, brings a wealth of experience and insight from civil society, the private sector, and the scientific community, underscoring the inclusive and comprehensive approach the UN is taking towards sustainable development,” an accompanying press statement noted. The other members of the group are Marian Dorcas Quain (Ghana), Deputy Director-General of CSIR Ghana; Giorgio Rossi (Italy), Vice-President of Elettra-Sincrotrone Trieste; Magnus Andersson (Sweden), Associate Professor at Malmö University; Mônica Tejo Cavalcanti (Brazil), Professor at the Federal University of Campina Grande; Evgeniya Dmitrieva (Russia), Member of the Civic Chamber of the Russian Federation; Motoko Kotani (Japan), Executive Director of Science at RIKEN; Jin Li (China), President of Fudan University; Madin Maseeh (Maldives), President of the Maldives Space Research Organisation; and Rita Orji (Nigeria), Canada Research Chair in Persuasive Technology at Dalhousie University. Professor Mande is also President of Vijnana Bharti, which, along with the Ministry of Science and Technology is gearing up to host the India International Science Festival in Pune in December. Announcing this on Wednesday (November 18, 2026), Union Minister of Science Jitendra Singh said at a press briefing that the government had taken a conscious decision to replace “scattered, repetitive gatherings”, including the erstwhile Indian Science Congress, with two flagship national events carrying distinct identities.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: While the Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave in October saw 13 Ministries and Nobel Laureates, and was an academic-driven conclave exploring frontier themes, the India International Science Festival (IISF) brought a “festive, public-facing character with international resonance”. By rotating the venue to different regions, after Chandigarh, Hyderabad, Goa and Delhi, bringing IISF for the first time to Pune leverages the western hub’s vibrant academic, research, and industrial ecosystem.

📚 TOP 4 HARD VOCABULARY WORDS EXTRACTED FROM THIS PARAGRAPH (TAP CARD FOR PICTURE & SYNONYMS):
Constitutional (Adjective)
संवैधानिक — देश के संविधान (Constitution) के दायरे और मौलिक अधिकारों के अनुरूप।
✓ Syn: Statutory, Legitimate, Lawful  |  ✖ Ant: Unconstitutional, Illegal, Arbitrary
Inclusive (Adjective)
समावेशी — जिसमें समाज के हर वर्ग (खासकर गरीब और वंचित वर्ग) को बराबर शामिल किया जाए।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Egalitarian, All-encompassing  |  ✖ Ant: Exclusive, Discriminatory, Narrow
Sustainability (Noun)
सतत विकास — पर्यावरण और भविष्य की पीढ़ियों को नुकसान पहुँचाए बिना लंबे समय तक चलने वाला विकास।
✓ Syn: Viability, Eco-balance, Durability  |  ✖ Ant: Depletion, Unsustainability, Destruction
International (Adjective)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'International' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🌐 International & Geopolitics passage on "UN Sustainable Development Goals group for science, technology rejigged", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. The group has been constituted even as the international community ramps up efforts to achieve the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'UN Sustainable Development Goals group for scien' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'UN Sustainable Development Goals group for sc' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'UN Sustainable Development Goals group for sc' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "The group has been constituted even as the international community ramps up efforts to achieve the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development." (Hinglish Arth: इस समूह का गठन तब किया गया है जब अंतर्राष्ट्रीय समुदाय सतत विकास के लिए 2030 एजेंडा को प्राप्त करने के प्रयासों में तेजी ला रहा है।)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "UN Sustainable Development Goals group for science, technology rejigged"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. By rotating the venue to different regions, after Chandigarh, Hyderabad, Goa and Delhi, bringing IISF for the first time to Pune leverages the...
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "By rotating the venue to different regions, after Chandigarh, Hyderabad, Goa and Delhi, bringing IISF for the first time to Pune leverages the..." (Hinglish Arth: चंडीगढ़, हैदराबाद, गोवा और दिल्ली के बाद आयोजन स्थल को विभिन्न क्षेत्रों में घुमाकर, आईआईएसएफ को पहली बार पुणे में लाने से पश्चिमी केंद्र के जीवंत शैक्षणिक, अनुसंधान और औद्योगिक पारिस्थितिकी तंत्र का लाभ मिलता है।)

articles.keyPoints:
• 1. Core Context & Background: The group has been constituted even as the international community ramps up efforts to achieve the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres has reconstituted a 10-member group that works on promoting science, technology and innovation toward achieving its Sustainable Development Goals. The lone Indian in this group is former biologist and former Council of Scientific and Industrial Research CSIR Director General, Shekhar Mande, who is also currently President, Indian National Science Academy. The group has been constituted even as the international community ramps up efforts to achieve the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, while preparing for the 2027 SDG Summit. “The group comprises distinguished experts from diverse geographic and disciplinary backgrounds from both developing and developed countries. Each member, recognised for their international excellence in science or technology, brings a wealth of experience and insight from civil society, the private sector, and the scientific community, underscoring the inclusive and comprehensive approach the UN is taking towards sustainable development,” an accompanying press statement noted. The other members of the group are Marian Dorcas Quain (Ghana), Deputy Director-General of CSIR Ghana; Giorgio Rossi (Italy), Vice-President of Elettra-Sincrotrone Trieste; Magnus Andersson (Sweden), Associate Professor at Malmö University; Mônica Tejo Cavalcanti (Brazil), Professor at the Federal University of Campina Grande; Evgeniya Dmitrieva (Russia), Member of the Civic Chamber of the Russian Federation; Motoko Kotani (Japan), Executive Director of Science at RIKEN; Jin Li (China), President of Fudan University; Madin Maseeh (Maldives), President of the Maldives Space Research Organisation; and Rita Orji (Nigeria), Canada Research Chair in Persuasive Technology at Dalhousie University. Professor Mande is also President of Vijnana Bharti, which, along with the Ministry of Science and Technology is gearing up to host the India International Science Festival in Pune in December. Announcing this on Wednesday (November 18, 2026), Union Minister of Science Jitendra Singh said at a press briefing that the government had taken a conscious decision to replace “scattered, repetitive gatherings”, including the erstwhile Indian Science Congress, with two flagship national events carrying distinct identities.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: While the Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave in October saw 13 Ministries and Nobel Laureates, and was an academic-driven conclave exploring frontier themes, the India International Science Festival (IISF) brought a “festive, public-facing character with international resonance”. By rotating the venue to different regions, after Chandigarh, Hyderabad, Goa and Delhi, bringing IISF for the first time to Pune leverages the western hub’s vibrant academic, research, and industrial ecosystem.

articles.title: Bangladesh deploys paramilitary as unrest grows over Hasina's return
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Police have recorded dozens of crude bomb blasts and incidents of vehicles ​being torched in at least ‌28 districts over the last 10 days, with several police personnel and civilians injured, local media has reported

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Bangladesh ‌stepped up security and deployed hundreds of paramilitary troops nationwide on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) ​as the planned return of former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has ⁠sparked clashes, bomb blasts, and arson attacks blamed on supporters of her banned party. Ms. Hasina, who has lived in exile in neighbouring India since she fled Dhaka following violent protests demanding ‌her resignation in August 2024, has requested a new passport and identity card, saying she plans to return in December. But the government ‌has so far rejected her request, leading to members and supporters of ‌her ⁠Awami League party taking to the streets in protest. Last week, the party ⁠announced a week-long programme of protests and rallies to mobilise support for Ms. Hasina's return, culminating in a nationwide lockdown on November 19. Police have recorded dozens of crude bomb blasts and incidents of vehicles ​being torched in at least ‌28 districts over the last 10 days, with several police personnel and civilians injured, local media has reported. Late on Tuesday (November 17, 2026), an activist of the ruling Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) was allegedly killed by unidentified people during a protest ‌near Ms. Hasina's home district of Gopalganj, police said. On the same night, a ​crude bomb exploded outside the Dhaka residence of Cultural Affairs Minister Nitai Roy Chowdhury, and the house of a BNP lawmaker and ⁠shops belonging to BNP supporters in Gopalganj were set on fire, police added. On Wednesday (November 18, 2026) morning, a bus company helper was burnt to death in the southern district ‌of Pirojpur after two buses were set on fire, authorities said. Tuesday (November 17, 2026) marked the day on which Ms. Hasina was sentenced to death a year ago by a local court that found her guilty of ordering a deadly crackdown on the student-led uprising against her in 2024.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: At least 37 Grameen Bank branches and offices have been targeted in arson attacks or attempted fires ‌since November 10, with 14 more attacked since midnight on Tuesday (November 17, 2026), the bank said.

📰 Bangladesh deploys paramilitary as unrest grows over Hasina's return

📌 Published: 18 Nov 2026, 11:13:26 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Police have recorded dozens of crude bomb blasts and incidents of vehicles ​being torched in at least ‌28 districts over the last 10 days, with several police personnel and civilians injured, local media has reported

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Bangladesh ‌stepped up security and deployed hundreds of paramilitary troops nationwide on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) ​as the planned return of former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has ⁠sparked clashes, bomb blasts, and arson attacks blamed on supporters of her banned party. Ms. Hasina, who has lived in exile in neighbouring India since she fled Dhaka following violent protests demanding ‌her resignation in August 2024, has requested a new passport and identity card, saying she plans to return in December. But the government ‌has so far rejected her request, leading to members and supporters of ‌her ⁠Awami League party taking to the streets in protest. Last week, the party ⁠announced a week-long programme of protests and rallies to mobilise support for Ms. Hasina's return, culminating in a nationwide lockdown on November 19. Police have recorded dozens of crude bomb blasts and incidents of vehicles ​being torched in at least ‌28 districts over the last 10 days, with several police personnel and civilians injured, local media has reported. Late on Tuesday (November 17, 2026), an activist of the ruling Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) was allegedly killed by unidentified people during a protest ‌near Ms. Hasina's home district of Gopalganj, police said. On the same night, a ​crude bomb exploded outside the Dhaka residence of Cultural Affairs Minister Nitai Roy Chowdhury, and the house of a BNP lawmaker and ⁠shops belonging to BNP supporters in Gopalganj were set on fire, police added. On Wednesday (November 18, 2026) morning, a bus company helper was burnt to death in the southern district ‌of Pirojpur after two buses were set on fire, authorities said. Tuesday (November 17, 2026) marked the day on which Ms. Hasina was sentenced to death a year ago by a local court that found her guilty of ordering a deadly crackdown on the student-led uprising against her in 2024.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: At least 37 Grameen Bank branches and offices have been targeted in arson attacks or attempted fires ‌since November 10, with 14 more attacked since midnight on Tuesday (November 17, 2026), the bank said.

articles.title: Saudis prepare for Houthi war to last well into 2027
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Saudi and Yemeni forces are ​now reorganising, with plans to protect Aden from the Houthi advances and potentially shift their offensive to eastern fronts where they have made some advances or have at least held their lines

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Saudi Arabia is preparing for war against Yemen's Houthis to stretch well into next year, doubling down despite setbacks on the battlefield in Yemen ​and attacks disrupting life at home, said two Western officials briefed by Saudis on the plans. The renewed conflict has become the most active front in ‌the wider Iran war, killing and wounding thousands and displacing hundreds of thousands in Yemen while derailing ​Saudi Arabia's efforts to draw in non-oil investment and host global events. Public messaging around the war has also ⁠slowly shifted in the kingdom, with greater acknowledgement of its impacts. Saudi officials now foresee the campaign stretching on for up to six months, aiming to see gains on the ground by the kingdom's Yemeni allies before any negotiations with the Houthis, according to Western officials, who spoke on condition ‌of anonymity to discuss non-public conversations with Saudi counterparts. A third source familiar with the Saudi plans confirmed the accounts. All three said a deal to end the wider Iran war could see the Yemen conflict draw down. The ‌third source also said Riyadh believes that U.S. offensive support for Saudi operations in Yemen, which President Donald Trump's administration has ‌so ⁠far withheld, could help change the tide of the conflict, potentially allowing Saudi-backed forces to make the gains ⁠they want within weeks. A Saudi Foreign Ministry official declined to comment on the views of Saudi officials as described by the Western officials. Saudi Arabia first entered the Yemen conflict in 2015 at the head of an Arab coalition to try to restore Yemen's government to power after the Houthis seized the ​capital Sanaa and much of the country. They fought to ‌a bloody stalemate and in 2022 reached a ceasefire that lasted until summer this year. Since fighting restarted, the Houthis have seized the Red Sea coast and strategic Bab el-Mandeb strait from Saudi-backed forces, and encircled the city of Taiz in highlands above the government's temporary capital Aden on the southern coast.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Yemeni government forces mounted a counterattack last month, recapturing territory around the ‌strait, but withdrew over the past weekend to protect Aden in a major setback.

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #23 of 30 (18 NOV)

📰 Saudis prepare for Houthi war to last well into 2027

📌 Published: 18 Nov 2026, 10:55:36 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Saudi and Yemeni forces are ​now reorganising, with plans to protect Aden from the Houthi advances and potentially shift their offensive to eastern fronts where they have made some advances or have at least held their lines

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Saudi Arabia is preparing for war against Yemen's Houthis to stretch well into next year, doubling down despite setbacks on the battlefield in Yemen ​and attacks disrupting life at home, said two Western officials briefed by Saudis on the plans. The renewed conflict has become the most active front in ‌the wider Iran war, killing and wounding thousands and displacing hundreds of thousands in Yemen while derailing ​Saudi Arabia's efforts to draw in non-oil investment and host global events. Public messaging around the war has also ⁠slowly shifted in the kingdom, with greater acknowledgement of its impacts. Saudi officials now foresee the campaign stretching on for up to six months, aiming to see gains on the ground by the kingdom's Yemeni allies before any negotiations with the Houthis, according to Western officials, who spoke on condition ‌of anonymity to discuss non-public conversations with Saudi counterparts. A third source familiar with the Saudi plans confirmed the accounts. All three said a deal to end the wider Iran war could see the Yemen conflict draw down. The ‌third source also said Riyadh believes that U.S. offensive support for Saudi operations in Yemen, which President Donald Trump's administration has ‌so ⁠far withheld, could help change the tide of the conflict, potentially allowing Saudi-backed forces to make the gains ⁠they want within weeks. A Saudi Foreign Ministry official declined to comment on the views of Saudi officials as described by the Western officials. Saudi Arabia first entered the Yemen conflict in 2015 at the head of an Arab coalition to try to restore Yemen's government to power after the Houthis seized the ​capital Sanaa and much of the country. They fought to ‌a bloody stalemate and in 2022 reached a ceasefire that lasted until summer this year. Since fighting restarted, the Houthis have seized the Red Sea coast and strategic Bab el-Mandeb strait from Saudi-backed forces, and encircled the city of Taiz in highlands above the government's temporary capital Aden on the southern coast.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Yemeni government forces mounted a counterattack last month, recapturing territory around the ‌strait, but withdrew over the past weekend to protect Aden in a major setback.

A. Saudi and Yemeni forces are ​now reorganising, with plans to protect Aden from the Houthi advances and potentially shift their offensive to eastern...
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Saudis prepare for Houthi war to last well into ' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Saudis prepare for Houthi war to last well in' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Saudis prepare for Houthi war to last well in' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Saudi and Yemeni forces are ​now reorganising, with plans to protect Aden from the Houthi advances and potentially shift their offensive to eastern..." (Hinglish Arth: सऊदी और यमनी सेनाएं अब पुनर्गठित हो रही हैं, अदन को हौथी अग्रिमों से बचाने की योजना बना रही हैं और संभावित रूप से अपने आक्रमण को पूर्वी मोर्चों पर स्थानांतरित कर रही हैं जहां उन्होंने कुछ प्रगति की है या कम से कम अपनी पकड़ बनाए रखी है।)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Saudis prepare for Houthi war to last well into 2027"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. Yemeni government forces mounted a counterattack last month, recapturing territory around the ‌strait, but withdrew over the past weekend to protect...
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "Yemeni government forces mounted a counterattack last month, recapturing territory around the ‌strait, but withdrew over the past weekend to protect..." (Hinglish Arth: यमनी सरकारी बलों ने पिछले महीने जवाबी हमला किया और जलडमरूमध्य के आसपास के क्षेत्र पर फिर से कब्जा कर लिया, लेकिन एक बड़े झटके में अदन की रक्षा के लिए पिछले सप्ताहांत में पीछे हट गए।)

articles.title: Ethiopia, Eritrea amass forces along border, heightening war fears: Sources
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The fighting in Tigray has stoked fears of a ​wider conflagration in the Horn of Africa, with Ethiopia’s government also accusing Sudan, which is in the midst of its own civil war, and Egypt of backing the rebels; Eritrea, Sudan, Egypt ⁠all deny doing so

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Ethiopia and Eritrea have amassed forces along their shared border, conflict monitors and people tied to militias in northern Ethiopia's Tigray ‌region said, fuelling fears of outright war between the historical rivals. The build-up along the border has brought ​the two armies within striking distance of each other, according to the conflict monitors ACLED and the International ⁠Crisis Group, a person close to a pro-Ethiopian government militia in Tigray, and another person close to anti-government rebels there. Reuters could not independently confirm reports of skirmishes between Ethiopian and Eritrean forces along the border. ACLED and a person close to the rebels said the ‌two sides had clashed in recent days, which would be their first direct armed exchanges in over a month, but the person close to the pro-Ethiopian government militia disputed this. Reached for comment, Eritrean Information ‌Minister Yemane Gebremeskel decried "propaganda" from Ethiopia's ruling party about developments near the border but did not directly address reports about ‌military ⁠build-ups or clashes. Spokespeople for the Ethiopian government did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Diplomats and ⁠experts have warned of possible conflict between Ethiopia and Eritrea since fighting broke out in September between Ethiopia’s federal government and rebels in Tigray, which borders Eritrea. Witnesses and Ethiopia's government said Eritrean forces crossed into Tigray in early October in support ​of the rebels. ACLED reported at the time ‌that drone strikes it believed were carried out by Ethiopia’s military had targeted the Eritrean troops. Ethiopia has not commented on the strikes. Eritrea has denied any incursion into Ethiopia and accused Addis Ababa of seeking a pretext to invade its smaller neighbour, which was an Ethiopian province for three decades before gaining independence in 1993. They are now separated ‌by a border stretching more than 1,000 km (620 miles). The fighting in Tigray has stoked fears of a ​wider conflagration in the Horn of Africa, with Ethiopia’s government also accusing Sudan, which is in the midst of its own civil war, and Egypt of backing the rebels. Eritrea, Sudan, and Egypt ⁠all deny doing so.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Ethiopia and Eritrea fought a border war from 1998 to 2000 that killed tens of thousands of people. The conflict was prompted by a dispute over the border town of Badme, which a UN boundary commission later found fell within Eritrean ‌territory.

Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Ethiopia, Eritrea amass forces along border, hei' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Ethiopia, Eritrea amass forces along border, ' should be permanently discontinued.

ultraAnalyticalQuestions2.answerText: The fighting in Tigray has stoked fears of a ​wider conflagration in the Horn of Africa, with Ethiopia’s government also accusing Sudan, which is in...

Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "The fighting in Tigray has stoked fears of a ​wider conflagration in the Horn of Africa, with Ethiopia’s government also accusing Sudan, which is in..." (Hinglish Arth: टाइग्रे में लड़ाई ने हॉर्न ऑफ अफ्रीका में व्यापक संघर्ष की आशंका पैदा कर दी है, इथियोपिया की सरकार ने सूडान पर भी आरोप लगाया है, जो अपने स्वयं के गृहयुद्ध के बीच में है, और मिस्र पर विद्रोहियों का समर्थन करने का आरोप लगाया गया है; इरीत्रे)

ultraAnalyticalQuestions2.badge: Analytical Q2 • Key Evidence, Policy & Way Forward
ultraAnalyticalQuestions2.question: Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Ethiopia, Eritrea amass forces along border, heightening war fears: Sources"?
options: Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
The conflict was prompted by a dispute over the border town of Badme, which a UN boundary commission later found fell within Eritrean ‌territory.
Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
ultraAnalyticalQuestions2.answerText: The conflict was prompted by a dispute over the border town of Badme, which a UN boundary commission later found fell within Eritrean ‌territory.
ultraAnalyticalQuestions2.hinglishExplanation: Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "The conflict was prompted by a dispute over the border town of Badme, which a UN boundary commission later found fell within Eritrean ‌territory." (Hinglish Arth: यह संघर्ष सीमावर्ती शहर बाडमे पर विवाद के कारण हुआ था, जिसे बाद में संयुक्त राष्ट्र सीमा आयोग ने इरिट्रिया क्षेत्र के अंतर्गत पाया था।)

hinglishTracks.en: The fighting in Tigray has stoked fears of a ​wider conflagration in the Horn of Africa, with Ethiopia’s government also accusing Sudan, which is in the midst of its own civil war, and Egypt of backing the rebels; Eritrea, Sudan, Egypt ⁠all deny doing so
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — टाइग्रे में लड़ाई ने हॉर्न ऑफ अफ्रीका में व्यापक संघर्ष की आशंका पैदा कर दी है, इथियोपिया की सरकार ने सूडान पर भी आरोप लगाया है, जो अपने स्वयं के गृहयुद्ध के बीच में है, और मिस्र पर विद्रोहियों का समर्थन करने का आरोप लगाया गया है; इरिट्रिया, सूडान, मिस्र सभी ऐसा करने से इनकार करते हैं। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Conflagration' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Conflagration' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Significant, Substantial, Strategic और Antonyms हैं: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial।

hinglishTracks.en: Ethiopia and Eritrea have amassed forces along their shared border, conflict monitors and people tied to militias in northern Ethiopia's Tigray ‌region said, fuelling fears of outright war between the historical rivals.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — इथियोपिया और इरिट्रिया ने अपनी साझा सीमा पर सेनाएं जमा कर ली हैं, संघर्ष पर नजर रखने वालों और उत्तरी इथियोपिया के टाइग्रे क्षेत्र में मिलिशिया से जुड़े लोगों ने कहा, जिससे ऐतिहासिक प्रतिद्वंद्वियों के बीच पूर्ण युद्ध की आशंका बढ़ गई है।।

hinglishTracks.en: The build-up along the border has brought ​the two armies within striking distance of each other, according to the conflict monitors ACLED and the International ⁠Crisis Group, a person close to a pro-Ethiopian government militia in Tigray, and another person close to anti-government rebels there.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — संघर्ष पर नजर रखने वाले एसीएलईडी और इंटरनेशनल क्राइसिस ग्रुप के अनुसार, सीमा पर निर्माण ने दोनों सेनाओं को एक-दूसरे से काफी दूरी पर ला दिया है, एक व्यक्ति टाइग्रे में इथियोपियाई सरकार समर्थक मिलिशिया का करीबी है, और एक अन्य व्यक्ति वहां सरकार विरोधी विद्रोहियों का करीबी है।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'International' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'International' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive और Antonyms हैं: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile।

hinglishTracks.en: Reuters could not independently confirm reports of skirmishes between Ethiopian and Eritrean forces along the border.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — रॉयटर्स सीमा पर इथियोपियाई और इरिट्रिया बलों के बीच झड़पों की रिपोर्ट की स्वतंत्र रूप से पुष्टि नहीं कर सका।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Independence' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: स्वतंत्रता — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Independence' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Restrictive, Counteractive, Adverse और Antonyms हैं: Constructive, Supportive, Favorable।

hinglishTracks.en: ACLED and a person close to the rebels said the ‌two sides had clashed in recent days, which would be their first direct armed exchanges in over a month, but the person close to the pro-Ethiopian government militia disputed this.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — एसीएलईडी और विद्रोहियों के करीबी एक व्यक्ति ने कहा कि दोनों पक्ष हाल के दिनों में भिड़ गए थे, जो एक महीने से अधिक समय में उनका पहला प्रत्यक्ष सशस्त्र आदान-प्रदान होगा, लेकिन इथियोपियाई सरकार समर्थक मिलिशिया के करीबी व्यक्ति ने इस पर विवाद किया।।

hinglishTracks.en: Reached for comment, Eritrean Information ‌Minister Yemane Gebremeskel decried "propaganda" from Ethiopia's ruling party about developments near the border but did not directly address reports about ‌military ⁠build-ups or clashes.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — टिप्पणी के लिए संपर्क किए जाने पर, इरिट्रिया के सूचना मंत्री यमने गेब्रेमेस्केल ने सीमा के निकट विकास के बारे में इथियोपिया की सत्तारूढ़ पार्टी के "प्रचार" की निंदा की, लेकिन सैन्य निर्माण या झड़पों के बारे में रिपोर्टों को सीधे तौर पर संबोधित नहीं किया।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Information' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Information' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Restrictive, Counteractive, Adverse और Antonyms हैं: Constructive, Supportive, Favorable।

hinglishTracks.en: Spokespeople for the Ethiopian government did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — इथियोपियाई सरकार के प्रवक्ताओं ने टिप्पणी के अनुरोधों का तुरंत जवाब नहीं दिया।।

hinglishTracks.en: Diplomats and ⁠experts have warned of possible conflict between Ethiopia and Eritrea since fighting broke out in September between Ethiopia’s federal government and rebels in Tigray, which borders Eritrea.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — सितंबर में इथियोपिया की संघीय सरकार और इरिट्रिया की सीमा से लगे टाइग्रे में विद्रोहियों के बीच लड़ाई शुरू होने के बाद से राजनयिकों और विशेषज्ञों ने इथियोपिया और इरिट्रिया के बीच संभावित संघर्ष की चेतावनी दी है।।

hinglishTracks.en: Witnesses and Ethiopia's government said Eritrean forces crossed into Tigray in early October in support ​of the rebels.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — प्रत्यक्षदर्शियों और इथियोपिया की सरकार ने कहा कि विद्रोहियों के समर्थन में इरिट्रिया की सेना अक्टूबर की शुरुआत में टाइग्रे में घुस गई।।

hinglishTracks.en: ACLED reported at the time ‌that drone strikes it believed were carried out by Ethiopia’s military had targeted the Eritrean troops.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — एसीएलईडी ने उस समय रिपोर्ट दी थी कि उसका मानना ​​है कि इथियोपिया की सेना द्वारा किए गए ड्रोन हमलों में इरिट्रिया के सैनिकों को निशाना बनाया गया था।।

hinglishTracks.en: Ethiopia has not commented on the strikes.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — इथियोपिया ने हमलों पर कोई टिप्पणी नहीं की है।।

hinglishTracks.en: Eritrea has denied any incursion into Ethiopia and accused Addis Ababa of seeking a pretext to invade its smaller neighbour, which was an Ethiopian province for three decades before gaining independence in 1993.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — इरिट्रिया ने इथियोपिया में किसी भी घुसपैठ से इनकार किया है और अदीस अबाबा पर अपने छोटे पड़ोसी पर आक्रमण करने का बहाना खोजने का आरोप लगाया है, जो 1993 में स्वतंत्रता प्राप्त करने से पहले तीन दशकों तक इथियोपियाई प्रांत था।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Independence' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: स्वतंत्रता — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Independence' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Restrictive, Counteractive, Adverse और Antonyms हैं: Constructive, Supportive, Favorable।

hinglishTracks.en: They are now separated ‌by a border stretching more than 1,000 km (620 miles).
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — वे अब 1,000 किमी (620 मील) से अधिक लंबी सीमा से अलग हो गए हैं।।

hinglishTracks.en: The fighting in Tigray has stoked fears of a ​wider conflagration in the Horn of Africa, with Ethiopia’s government also accusing Sudan, which is in the midst of its own civil war, and Egypt of backing the rebels.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — टाइग्रे में लड़ाई ने हॉर्न ऑफ अफ्रीका में व्यापक संघर्ष की आशंका पैदा कर दी है, इथियोपिया की सरकार ने सूडान पर भी आरोप लगाया है, जो अपने स्वयं के गृहयुद्ध के बीच में है, और मिस्र पर विद्रोहियों का समर्थन करने का आरोप लगाया गया है।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Conflagration' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Conflagration' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Significant, Substantial, Strategic और Antonyms हैं: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial।

hinglishTracks.en: Eritrea, Sudan, and Egypt ⁠all deny doing so.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — इरिट्रिया, सूडान और मिस्र सभी ऐसा करने से इनकार करते हैं।।

hinglishTracks.en: Ethiopia and Eritrea fought a border war from 1998 to 2000 that killed tens of thousands of people.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — इथियोपिया और इरिट्रिया ने 1998 से 2000 तक सीमा युद्ध लड़ा जिसमें हजारों लोग मारे गए।।

hinglishTracks.en: The conflict was prompted by a dispute over the border town of Badme, which a UN boundary commission later found fell within Eritrean ‌territory.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — यह संघर्ष सीमावर्ती शहर बाडमे पर विवाद के कारण हुआ था, जिसे बाद में संयुक्त राष्ट्र सीमा आयोग ने इरिट्रिया क्षेत्र के अंतर्गत पाया था।।

articles.newspaperPrintHtml:
🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #24 of 30 (18 NOV)

📰 Ethiopia, Eritrea amass forces along border, heightening war fears: Sources

📌 Published: 18 Nov 2026, 10:53:13 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The fighting in Tigray has stoked fears of a ​wider conflagration in the Horn of Africa, with Ethiopia’s government also accusing Sudan, which is in the midst of its own civil war, and Egypt of backing the rebels; Eritrea, Sudan, Egypt ⁠all deny doing so

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Ethiopia and Eritrea have amassed forces along their shared border, conflict monitors and people tied to militias in northern Ethiopia's Tigray ‌region said, fuelling fears of outright war between the historical rivals. The build-up along the border has brought ​the two armies within striking distance of each other, according to the conflict monitors ACLED and the International ⁠Crisis Group, a person close to a pro-Ethiopian government militia in Tigray, and another person close to anti-government rebels there. Reuters could not independently confirm reports of skirmishes between Ethiopian and Eritrean forces along the border. ACLED and a person close to the rebels said the ‌two sides had clashed in recent days, which would be their first direct armed exchanges in over a month, but the person close to the pro-Ethiopian government militia disputed this. Reached for comment, Eritrean Information ‌Minister Yemane Gebremeskel decried "propaganda" from Ethiopia's ruling party about developments near the border but did not directly address reports about ‌military ⁠build-ups or clashes. Spokespeople for the Ethiopian government did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Diplomats and ⁠experts have warned of possible conflict between Ethiopia and Eritrea since fighting broke out in September between Ethiopia’s federal government and rebels in Tigray, which borders Eritrea. Witnesses and Ethiopia's government said Eritrean forces crossed into Tigray in early October in support ​of the rebels. articles.title: Trump's Board of Peace faults Israel, Hamas for failure to end Gaza war
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: While the ceasefire has halted major fighting, the wider plan, which calls for Hamas ⁠to disarm, Israeli troops to withdraw and reconstruction to begin, has effectively stalled since soon after it came into effect last year

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The body overseeing U.S. President Donald Trump's plan to end the Gaza ‌war accused both Israel and Hamas of failing to meet their commitments to end hostilities, leaving ​the population of Gaza in dire conditions and the ceasefire in danger of collapse. The 12-page Board ⁠of Peace report, seen by Reuters , is the body's second to the United Nations Security Council since the U.S.-backed ceasefire came into effect 13 months ago. It offers a sobering assessment of progress made since then. The Board, established and headed by Mr. Trump, is expected ‌to present the report's findings to a meeting of the council in New York at the end of November. "The distance between what has been agreed and what is happening on the ground nonetheless remains ‌the principal risk to the process," the report said, warning that "a ceasefire that delivers nothing visible cannot be ‌sustained ⁠indefinitely." While the ceasefire has halted major fighting, the wider plan, which calls for Hamas ⁠to disarm, Israeli troops to withdraw and reconstruction to begin, has effectively stalled since soon after it came into effect last year. Hamas agreed in July to a Board of Peace roadmap to surrender its weapons and transfer governance of Gaza to a civilian transitional authority, but Israel rejected ​the roadmap, saying it will not withdraw until Hamas ‌is dismantled. Israel has carried out near-daily strikes on Gaza, while the report said Hamas fighters have also continued attacks on Israeli troops. "Every day that Israel continues strikes against Hamas targets, it delays putting Hamas' agreement to the roadmap to the test," the report said. "Meanwhile, Hamas militant activity continues, the commitment to cease all military activities has not ‌been met in full by the parties, and the population faces another winter in tents and rubble."

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Senior Hamas ​official Basem Naim dismissed the report as "pure disinformation", accusing the Board of Peace of providing cover to Israel to evade its commitments under the plan to end the war and to ⁠continue its aggression in Gaza.

📰 Trump's Board of Peace faults Israel, Hamas for failure to end Gaza war

📌 Published: 18 Nov 2026, 10:51:18 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: While the ceasefire has halted major fighting, the wider plan, which calls for Hamas ⁠to disarm, Israeli troops to withdraw and reconstruction to begin, has effectively stalled since soon after it came into effect last year

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The body overseeing U.S. President Donald Trump's plan to end the Gaza ‌war accused both Israel and Hamas of failing to meet their commitments to end hostilities, leaving ​the population of Gaza in dire conditions and the ceasefire in danger of collapse. The 12-page Board ⁠of Peace report, seen by Reuters , is the body's second to the United Nations Security Council since the U.S.-backed ceasefire came into effect 13 months ago. It offers a sobering assessment of progress made since then. The Board, established and headed by Mr. Trump, is expected ‌to present the report's findings to a meeting of the council in New York at the end of November. "The distance between what has been agreed and what is happening on the ground nonetheless remains ‌the principal risk to the process," the report said, warning that "a ceasefire that delivers nothing visible cannot be ‌sustained ⁠indefinitely." While the ceasefire has halted major fighting, the wider plan, which calls for Hamas ⁠to disarm, Israeli troops to withdraw and reconstruction to begin, has effectively stalled since soon after it came into effect last year. Hamas agreed in July to a Board of Peace roadmap to surrender its weapons and transfer governance of Gaza to a civilian transitional authority, but Israel rejected ​the roadmap, saying it will not withdraw until Hamas ‌is dismantled. Israel has carried out near-daily strikes on Gaza, while the report said Hamas fighters have also continued attacks on Israeli troops. "Every day that Israel continues strikes against Hamas targets, it delays putting Hamas' agreement to the roadmap to the test," the report said. "Meanwhile, Hamas militant activity continues, the commitment to cease all military activities has not ‌been met in full by the parties, and the population faces another winter in tents and rubble."

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Senior Hamas ​official Basem Naim dismissed the report as "pure disinformation", accusing the Board of Peace of providing cover to Israel to evade its commitments under the plan to end the war and to ⁠continue its aggression in Gaza.

articles.title: India, Canada eye defence pact during Modi visit in December
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: India’s High Commissioner to Ottawa says both countries cannot afford to let fringe issues derail their extensive mutual interests

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: India and Canada could be announcing a defence agreement during Prime Minister Narendra Modi ’s official visit in December, according to the country’s High Commissioner to Ottawa, Dinesh K. Patnaik. Both countries are also in the final stages of negotiations of a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement. “We are on the cusp of finalising it,” Mr. Patnaik said. Addressing a gathering in the Canadian capital organised by the Centre for Strategic Statecraft and the Canadian International Council, he said that both countries cannot afford to let fringe issues derail their extensive mutual interests. Mr. Patnaik took over as India’s High Commissioner to Ottawa in September 2025. Both countries had earlier expelled each other’s High Commissioners and reduced their diplomatic presence following the murder of Sikh Khalistani activist Hardeep Singh Nijjar in June 2023. Then Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau accused India of orchestrating the murder, throwing bilateral relations into a tailspin. Subsequent reports by Canadian agencies also listed India, alongside China and Russia, as an interferer in domestic politics. The turnaround in ties, which began with the mutual reinstatement of High Commissioners, is set to reach a milestone with Mr. Modi’s visit on December 11 and 12. Mr. Patnaik said India and Canada are no longer talking about a reset of their derailed relations, but rather an overarching boost in ties spanning defence, space, nuclear energy, deep tech, trade, and the mobility of people. The two nations have moved from a complete lack of trust over a year ago to an unprecedented degree of mutual trust, he added. “The fact is that in the core strategic concerns of Canada and India, there is no conflict. Still, all it took for the entire bilateral relationship to be derailed was the fringe diaspora issue,” he said, referring to the murder of Nijjar. “The reason was the lack of trust. India believed that Canada was actively promoting separatism in India, and Canada believed India was organising violence in Canada. We had a series of meetings between senior Ministers, NSAs of both countries, and agencies at all levels as we set about rebuilding trust. Today, we have reached the highest levels of trust, where the most sensitive areas of cooperation, such as deep tech, defence, and space, are subjects of mutual cooperation,” Mr. Patnaik said. Cooperation between Canadian and Indian agencies remains at a high level, the High Commissioner added.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Canada / politics / politics (general) / defence / national politics

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #24 of 30 (18 NOV)

📰 India, Canada eye defence pact during Modi visit in December

📌 Published: 18 Nov 2026, 10:46:14 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: India’s High Commissioner to Ottawa says both countries cannot afford to let fringe issues derail their extensive mutual interests

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: India and Canada could be announcing a defence agreement during Prime Minister Narendra Modi ’s official visit in December, according to the country’s High Commissioner to Ottawa, Dinesh K. Patnaik. Both countries are also in the final stages of negotiations of a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement. “We are on the cusp of finalising it,” Mr. Patnaik said. Addressing a gathering in the Canadian capital organised by the Centre for Strategic Statecraft and the Canadian International Council, he said that both countries cannot afford to let fringe issues derail their extensive mutual interests. Mr. Patnaik took over as India’s High Commissioner to Ottawa in September 2025. Both countries had earlier expelled each other’s High Commissioners and reduced their diplomatic presence following the murder of Sikh Khalistani activist Hardeep Singh Nijjar in June 2023. Then Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau accused India of orchestrating the murder, throwing bilateral relations into a tailspin. Subsequent reports by Canadian agencies also listed India, alongside China and Russia, as an interferer in domestic politics. The turnaround in ties, which began with the mutual reinstatement of High Commissioners, is set to reach a milestone with Mr. Modi’s visit on December 11 and 12. Mr. Patnaik said India and Canada are no longer talking about a reset of their derailed relations, but rather an overarching boost in ties spanning defence, space, nuclear energy, deep tech, trade, and the mobility of people. The two nations have moved from a complete lack of trust over a year ago to an unprecedented degree of mutual trust, he added. “The fact is that in the core strategic concerns of Canada and India, there is no conflict. Still, all it took for the entire bilateral relationship to be derailed was the fringe diaspora issue,” he said, referring to the murder of Nijjar. “The reason was the lack of trust. India believed that Canada was actively promoting separatism in India, and Canada believed India was organising violence in Canada. We had a series of meetings between senior Ministers, NSAs of both countries, and agencies at all levels as we set about rebuilding trust. Today, we have reached the highest levels of trust, where the most sensitive areas of cooperation, such as deep tech, defence, and space, are subjects of mutual cooperation,” Mr. Patnaik said. Cooperation between Canadian and Indian agencies remains at a high level, the High Commissioner added.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Canada / politics / politics (general) / defence / national politics

articles.keyPoints:
• 1. Core Context & Background: India’s High Commissioner to Ottawa says both countries cannot afford to let fringe issues derail their extensive mutual interests
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: India and Canada could be announcing a defence agreement during Prime Minister Narendra Modi ’s official visit in December, according to the country’s High Commissioner to Ottawa, Dinesh K. Patnaik. Both countries are also in the final stages of negotiations of a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement. “We are on the cusp of finalising it,” Mr. Patnaik said. Addressing a gathering in the Canadian capital organised by the Centre for Strategic Statecraft and the Canadian International Council, he said that both countries cannot afford to let fringe issues derail their extensive mutual interests. Mr. Patnaik took over as India’s High Commissioner to Ottawa in September 2025. Both countries had earlier expelled each other’s High Commissioners and reduced their diplomatic presence following the murder of Sikh Khalistani activist Hardeep Singh Nijjar in June 2023. Then Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau accused India of orchestrating the murder, throwing bilateral relations into a tailspin. Subsequent reports by Canadian agencies also listed India, alongside China and Russia, as an interferer in domestic politics. The turnaround in ties, which began with the mutual reinstatement of High Commissioners, is set to reach a milestone with Mr. Modi’s visit on December 11 and 12. Mr. Patnaik said India and Canada are no longer talking about a reset of their derailed relations, but rather an overarching boost in ties spanning defence, space, nuclear energy, deep tech, trade, and the mobility of people. The two nations have moved from a complete lack of trust over a year ago to an unprecedented degree of mutual trust, he added. “The fact is that in the core strategic concerns of Canada and India, there is no conflict. Still, all it took for the entire bilateral relationship to be derailed was the fringe diaspora issue,” he said, referring to the murder of Nijjar. “The reason was the lack of trust. India believed that Canada was actively promoting separatism in India, and Canada believed India was organising violence in Canada. We had a series of meetings between senior Ministers, NSAs of both countries, and agencies at all levels as we set about rebuilding trust. Today, we have reached the highest levels of trust, where the most sensitive areas of cooperation, such as deep tech, defence, and space, are subjects of mutual cooperation,” Mr. Patnaik said. Cooperation between Canadian and Indian agencies remains at a high level, the High Commissioner added.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Canada / politics / politics (general) / defence / national politics

articles.title: Scientists warn of growing health threats of chemicals found everywhere
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: EDCs are chemicals that interfere with, mimic, or block the hormones that regulate the development and behaviour of our organs

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Chemicals found almost everywhere in modern life pose a "global and growing threat" to human health and the environment, a landmark report based on over a decade of research has warned. The report on "endocrine-disrupting chemicals" (EDCs) released by the United Nations Environment Programme and World Health Organization "conservatively" estimates the health and environmental costs of EDC exposure at over $1 trillion annually. "The scientific evidence is clear: EDCs are a global and growing threat to human and environmental health," warns the report written by international scientists, calling current regulations "uneven and insufficient." EDCs are chemicals that interfere with, mimic, or block the hormones that regulate the development and behaviour of our organs. They are in everything from toys and makeup, to building materials and clothing. The report released late Tuesday is the first such comprehensive look at EDC impacts in 14 years, and finds increasingly clear links between them and a range of diseases. "The evidence is so strong that it's irrefutable at this point," said Laura Vandenberg, report co-author and professor of environmental health sciences at the University of Massachusetts Amherst. The report examined thousands of studies on chemicals like bisphenols, phthalates and parabens. Evidence of links between these chemicals and disease is strongest for certain neurological conditions and reproductive problems including sperm decline.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: But there is also growing confidence that EDCs are linked to diseases like type 2 diabetes and asthma that have spiked globally.

articles.keyPoints:
• 1. Core Context & Background: EDCs are chemicals that interfere with, mimic, or block the hormones that regulate the development and behaviour of our organs
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Chemicals found almost everywhere in modern life pose a "global and growing threat" to human health and the environment, a landmark report based on over a decade of research has warned. The report on "endocrine-disrupting chemicals" (EDCs) released by the United Nations Environment Programme and World Health Organization "conservatively" estimates the health and environmental costs of EDC exposure at over $1 trillion annually. "The scientific evidence is clear: EDCs are a global and growing threat to human and environmental health," warns the report written by international scientists, calling current regulations "uneven and insufficient." EDCs are chemicals that interfere with, mimic, or block the hormones that regulate the development and behaviour of our organs. They are in everything from toys and makeup, to building materials and clothing. The report released late Tuesday is the first such comprehensive look at EDC impacts in 14 years, and finds increasingly clear links between them and a range of diseases. "The evidence is so strong that it's irrefutable at this point," said Laura Vandenberg, report co-author and professor of environmental health sciences at the University of Massachusetts Amherst. The report examined thousands of studies on chemicals like bisphenols, phthalates and parabens. Evidence of links between these chemicals and disease is strongest for certain neurological conditions and reproductive problems including sperm decline.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: But there is also growing confidence that EDCs are linked to diseases like type 2 diabetes and asthma that have spiked globally.

articles.title: Researchers boost gut microbial activity linked to longevity in aged mice, find improved metabolism
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The study suggests that specific age-related changes in the gut microbiome may be protective adaptations rather than signs of decline, and could potentially be harnessed to support healthier ageing

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Researchers have identified changes in the metabolic activity of the gut microbiome associated with exceptional longevity in humans, and found that amplifying the same activity in aged mice using engineered bacteria improved metabolic health. Published in the journal Cell Metabolism , the team's study suggests that specific age-related changes in the gut microbiome may be protective adaptations rather than signs of decline, and could potentially be harnessed to support healthier aging. Senior author Amir Zarrinpar, chair in circadian biology and medicine, and professor of medicine at the University of California San Diego, said while many studies on aging focus on what goes wrong as one grows old, the findings suggest "some changes in the gut microbiome may actually represent the body's attempt to preserve metabolic health". "If we can identify those beneficial functions and safely strengthen them, we may eventually be able to develop new ways to promote healthier aging," Zarrinpar said. The gut microbiome, the community of bacteria and other microbes living in the digestive tract, is known to change throughout life and plays an important role in metabolism and inflammation, among other aspects of health. Studies have also found distinctive microbiome features among people who age exceptionally well. The researchers focused on how gut microbes modify bile acids, substances produced by the liver that help digest fats but also act as signalling molecules in the body. Studying young and aged mice, they found that aging was associated with an increased microbial activity linked to enzymes called bile salt hydrolases. These enzymes chemically modify bile acids, allowing them to influence pathways involved in metabolism, inflammation and the body's internal clock. The team also found greater bile acid modification in the mice.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: To determine patterns in humans, they reanalysed publicly available data from a human ageing cohort, analysing bile acid measurements from 48 young adults, 107 older adults and 125 centenarians.

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #27 of 30 (18 NOV)

📰 Researchers boost gut microbial activity linked to longevity in aged mice, find improved metabolism

📌 Published: 18 Nov 2026, 07:53:42 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The study suggests that specific age-related changes in the gut microbiome may be protective adaptations rather than signs of decline, and could potentially be harnessed to support healthier ageing

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Researchers have identified changes in the metabolic activity of the gut microbiome associated with exceptional longevity in humans, and found that amplifying the same activity in aged mice using engineered bacteria improved metabolic health. Published in the journal Cell Metabolism , the team's study suggests that specific age-related changes in the gut microbiome may be protective adaptations rather than signs of decline, and could potentially be harnessed to support healthier aging. Senior author Amir Zarrinpar, chair in circadian biology and medicine, and professor of medicine at the University of California San Diego, said while many studies on aging focus on what goes wrong as one grows old, the findings suggest "some changes in the gut microbiome may actually represent the body's attempt to preserve metabolic health". "If we can identify those beneficial functions and safely strengthen them, we may eventually be able to develop new ways to promote healthier aging," Zarrinpar said. The gut microbiome, the community of bacteria and other microbes living in the digestive tract, is known to change throughout life and plays an important role in metabolism and inflammation, among other aspects of health. Studies have also found distinctive microbiome features among people who age exceptionally well. The researchers focused on how gut microbes modify bile acids, substances produced by the liver that help digest fats but also act as signalling molecules in the body. Studying young and aged mice, they found that aging was associated with an increased microbial activity linked to enzymes called bile salt hydrolases. These enzymes chemically modify bile acids, allowing them to influence pathways involved in metabolism, inflammation and the body's internal clock. The team also found greater bile acid modification in the mice.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: To determine patterns in humans, they reanalysed publicly available data from a human ageing cohort, analysing bile acid measurements from 48 young adults, 107 older adults and 125 centenarians.

articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Indian laws protect the decision not to have a child through statutes, schemes and subsidies, but the decision to have one is left to the mercy of the private assisted reproduction healthcare market

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The reproductive-autonomy jurisprudence as evolved by the Supreme Court under Article 21 of the Constitution is rich yet narrow, focusing primarily on one side of the problem. In Suchita Srivastava v. Chandigarh Administration (2009), the Court held that reproductive choices may be exercised to procreate as well as to abstain from procreating. In X v. Principal Secretary, Health and Family Welfare Department (2022), the Supreme Court extended the right to abortion to unmarried women as an exercise of ‘decisional autonomy’.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: These, and nearly all other landmark cases are concerned only with an existing pregnancy. The freedom to pursue parenthood through medical treatment, however, has surfaced only at the margins. The Delhi High Court, in 2023, allowed parole of a life convict to attempt IVF, by recognising a “right to parenthood,” but only as a claim against a barrier the State itself had erected. No court has yet asked whether the State may leave a citizen’s access to infertility care entirely to their own purse. Can a right available to the fertile but structurally withheld from the infertile be called a universal right?

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #28 of 30 (18 NOV)

📰 Does India need to financially aid families’ decisions to have a child through fertility treatment?

📌 Published: 18 Nov 2026, 07:51:54 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Indian laws protect the decision not to have a child through statutes, schemes and subsidies, but the decision to have one is left to the mercy of the private assisted reproduction healthcare market

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The reproductive-autonomy jurisprudence as evolved by the Supreme Court under Article 21 of the Constitution is rich yet narrow, focusing primarily on one side of the problem. In Suchita Srivastava v. Chandigarh Administration (2009), the Court held that reproductive choices may be exercised to procreate as well as to abstain from procreating. In X v. Principal Secretary, Health and Family Welfare Department (2022), the Supreme Court extended the right to abortion to unmarried women as an exercise of ‘decisional autonomy’.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: These, and nearly all other landmark cases are concerned only with an existing pregnancy. The freedom to pursue parenthood through medical treatment, however, has surfaced only at the margins. The Delhi High Court, in 2023, allowed parole of a life convict to attempt IVF, by recognising a “right to parenthood,” but only as a claim against a barrier the State itself had erected. No court has yet asked whether the State may leave a citizen’s access to infertility care entirely to their own purse. Can a right available to the fertile but structurally withheld from the infertile be called a universal right?

articles.title: Cyclone Akvan: why is Andhra Pradesh facing a third cyclone in a month?
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Warm seas, river water that traps heat near the surface and winds that steer storms towards the coast have made this post-monsoon season unusual, experts say

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Andhra Pradesh is currently facing a rare weather phenomenon. Since October 28, the State has already been hit by two back-to-back cyclonic storms, and there is an imminent threat of another one battering the coastal districts in the next two days. On October 28, the State was battered by very severe cyclonic storm Arnab , which made landfall near Narsapur in West Godavari district. On November 3, it was hit again by severe cyclonic storm Murasu , which made landfall close to Ongole in Prakasam district. Now, cyclonic storm Akvan is likely to intensify into a very severe cyclonic storm and make landfall on November 20 between Narsapur and Puri. Three tropical storms battering the coast within less than a month during the post-monsoon season is a rare scenario. The last times such a thing happened were in 1976, 1987 and 2013. Both 1976 and 1987 were El Niño years, and this year is also categorised as a super El Niño year . When it comes to tropical cyclones over the Bay of Bengal, there are a number of driving factors, and El Niño is just one of them. Mostly, the formation of storms over the Bay, especially their frequency and intensity, differs slightly from the rest of the world, because the Bay of Bengal is almost a land-locked sea, said S.S.V.S. Ramakrishna, former head of the Department of Oceanography and Meteorology, Andhra University, who has spent over four decades researching the pattern of cyclones over the Bay. “El Niño typically suppresses the southwest summer monsoon over India, but it has the opposite effect on the Northeast (winter) Monsoon and post-monsoon cyclogenesis in the Bay of Bengal,” he said. El Niño drought then floods hit North Andhra farmers El Niño, a deficient monsoon, and the heat to come During El Niño years, the northeast monsoon tends to be significantly more active over southern peninsular India. This creates continuous moisture convergence and frequent convective disturbances over the southern Bay, providing a steady assembly line of low-pressure areas. And sometimes, in rare occurrences, remnants of a Pacific Ocean cyclone cross the Strait of Malacca, re-enter the Bay of Bengal, and intensify into a cyclone. “We had seen this phenomenon during the Odisha Super Cyclone in 1999,” he said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Mr. Ramakrishna also pointed out that in October and November, the Bay of Bengal consistently retained high sea surface temperatures—over 26.5 degrees Celsius—and anything above 26 is conducive to developing a cyclonic system. This has been aided by the El Niño-modified upper-level wind patterns over the southern Bay of Bengal, which reduce vertical wind shear.

hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — इसे दक्षिणी बंगाल की खाड़ी के ऊपर अल नीनो-संशोधित ऊपरी-स्तरीय पवन पैटर्न से सहायता मिली है, जो ऊर्ध्वाधर पवन कतरनी को कम करता है।।

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #29 of 30 (18 NOV)

📰 Cyclone Akvan: why is Andhra Pradesh facing a third cyclone in a month?

📌 Published: 18 Nov 2026, 06:23:54 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Warm seas, river water that traps heat near the surface and winds that steer storms towards the coast have made this post-monsoon season unusual, experts say

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Andhra Pradesh is currently facing a rare weather phenomenon. Since October 28, the State has already been hit by two back-to-back cyclonic storms, and there is an imminent threat of another one battering the coastal districts in the next two days. On October 28, the State was battered by very severe cyclonic storm Arnab , which made landfall near Narsapur in West Godavari district. On November 3, it was hit again by severe cyclonic storm Murasu , which made landfall close to Ongole in Prakasam district. Now, cyclonic storm Akvan is likely to intensify into a very severe cyclonic storm and make landfall on November 20 between Narsapur and Puri. Three tropical storms battering the coast within less than a month during the post-monsoon season is a rare scenario. The last times such a thing happened were in 1976, 1987 and 2013. Both 1976 and 1987 were El Niño years, and this year is also categorised as a super El Niño year . When it comes to tropical cyclones over the Bay of Bengal, there are a number of driving factors, and El Niño is just one of them. Mostly, the formation of storms over the Bay, especially their frequency and intensity, differs slightly from the rest of the world, because the Bay of Bengal is almost a land-locked sea, said S.S.V.S. Ramakrishna, former head of the Department of Oceanography and Meteorology, Andhra University, who has spent over four decades researching the pattern of cyclones over the Bay. “El Niño typically suppresses the southwest summer monsoon over India, but it has the opposite effect on the Northeast (winter) Monsoon and post-monsoon cyclogenesis in the Bay of Bengal,” he said. El Niño drought then floods hit North Andhra farmers El Niño, a deficient monsoon, and the heat to come During El Niño years, the northeast monsoon tends to be significantly more active over southern peninsular India. This creates continuous moisture convergence and frequent convective disturbances over the southern Bay, providing a steady assembly line of low-pressure areas. And sometimes, in rare occurrences, remnants of a Pacific Ocean cyclone cross the Strait of Malacca, re-enter the Bay of Bengal, and intensify into a cyclone. “We had seen this phenomenon during the Odisha Super Cyclone in 1999,” he said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Mr. Ramakrishna also pointed out that in October and November, the Bay of Bengal consistently retained high sea surface temperatures—over 26.5 degrees Celsius—and anything above 26 is conducive to developing a cyclonic system. This has been aided by the El Niño-modified upper-level wind patterns over the southern Bay of Bengal, which reduce vertical wind shear.

Meteorological (Adjective)
मौसम विज्ञान और वायुमंडलीय परिवर्तनों से संबंधित (Connected with weather forecasting and atmospheric shifts).
✓ Syn: Atmospheric, Climatic, Weather-related  |  ✖ Ant: Geological, Subterranean, Terrestrial
Convergence (Noun)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Convergence' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Department (Adjective)
विभाग — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Department' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
University (Adjective / Verb)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'University' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Restrictive, Counteractive, Adverse  |  ✖ Ant: Constructive, Supportive, Favorable

Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🚀 Science, Tech & Environment passage on "Cyclone Akvan: why is Andhra Pradesh facing a third cyclone in a month?", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. Warm seas, river water that traps heat near the surface and winds that steer storms towards the coast have made this post-monsoon season unusual,...
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Cyclone Akvan: why is Andhra Pradesh facing a th' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Cyclone Akvan: why is Andhra Pradesh facing a' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Cyclone Akvan: why is Andhra Pradesh facing a' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Warm seas, river water that traps heat near the surface and winds that steer storms towards the coast have made this post-monsoon season unusual,..."
