1. Core Context & Background: The statement comes after an online petition to reinstate Huang gathered more than 1,90,000 signatures, including from tech industry figures like SpaceX and Tesla CEO Elon Musk

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has signalled his interest in returning to lead the AI computer chip company in his first public statement since he abruptly left the company last week following revelations of an extramarital affair with an alleged Chinese spy . “If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honoured to answer these calls and return as CEO,” he said in a social media post. He acknowledged making “serious mistakes” in his personal life but said that he’s received an “outpouring” of support from employees, investors, business partners and customers for his return. The statement comes after an online petition to reinstate Mr. Huang gathered more than 1,90,000 signatures, including from tech industry figures like SpaceX and Tesla CEO Elon Musk. President Donald Trump also endorsed the bid. Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Mr. Huang’s statement. Also on Tuesday (November 17, 2026), key House lawmakers said that Mr. Huang has voluntarily agreed to appear for transcribed interviews as the chipmaker faces intensifying national scrutiny over sales of its advanced computer chips. articles.title: U.K. sanctions Israeli companies building West Bank settlements
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The long-discussed E1 project would effectively cut off eastern Jerusalem from Palestinian population centres in the occupied West Bank, harming the prospects for a viable independent Palestinian state, Britain says

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The UK has sanctioned Israeli construction and property development companies it says are involved in building West Bank settlements, the first concrete step in Britain's previously announced effort to slow the expansion of settlements and preserve the possibility of a two-state solution to the Israeli-Palestinian conflict. The sanctions are the first announced since Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said Sept. 8 that Britain would toughen its stance toward its longtime ally. His announcement followed Israel's decision to seek bids to build 1,200 homes in the E1 area east of Jerusalem and an increase in settler attacks on Palestinians in the West Bank. The long-discussed E1 project would effectively cut off eastern Jerusalem from Palestinian population centres in the occupied West Bank, harming the prospects for a viable independent Palestinian state, Britain says. “Illegal settlement expansion in the West Bank is destroying the prospects of a two-state solution, so today we are sanctioning companies involved in this activity and disrupting their access to the finance that enables it,” Miliband said in a video posted on X. “And our warning to companies thinking about being part of settlement expansion, including the unconscionable E1 project, is clear: We will clamp down on you.” Britain has long been one of Israel's staunchest allies. Miliband recently described himself as a “proud British Jew” whose grandmother survived the Holocaust. But the U.K. government has grown increasingly critical of Israel's government as the war in Gaza has drawn tens of thousands of protesters onto the streets of London and other cities. Earlier this year, Britain joined five other Western countries in imposing additional sanctions on settlers and settlements. The latest measures target eight property development and construction firms, as well as Tzav 9, an Israeli activist movement that has blocked humanitarian aid convoys from entering Gaza, the government said. The companies are Har Hevron Development Co., Hemdat Shomron, S.A.G. (Velvel) Construction and Development, Lev HaHar Yazamut, Harey Zahav, Ariel Residential Judea & Samaria, Ami Gvirtzman Architects 2021 and Z.F. Building Co. All eight companies and Tzav 9 are now subject to UK asset freezes, and people associated with them will be barred from serving as directors of UK-based companies.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Announcing Britain's plans Sept. 8, Miliband said Israel had crossed a “long-standing red line” by advancing the E1 project. First proposed in the 1990s, it has been repeatedly delayed by international opposition. Israel's outgoing government, dominated by settler leaders, has begun seeking bids to build several thousand homes.

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #22 of 30 (17 NOV)

📰 U.K. sanctions Israeli companies building West Bank settlements

📌 Published: 17 Nov 2026, 11:41:03 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The long-discussed E1 project would effectively cut off eastern Jerusalem from Palestinian population centres in the occupied West Bank, harming the prospects for a viable independent Palestinian state, Britain says

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The UK has sanctioned Israeli construction and property development companies it says are involved in building West Bank settlements, the first concrete step in Britain's previously announced effort to slow the expansion of settlements and preserve the possibility of a two-state solution to the Israeli-Palestinian conflict. The sanctions are the first announced since Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said Sept. 8 that Britain would toughen its stance toward its longtime ally. His announcement followed Israel's decision to seek bids to build 1,200 homes in the E1 area east of Jerusalem and an increase in settler attacks on Palestinians in the West Bank. The long-discussed E1 project would effectively cut off eastern Jerusalem from Palestinian population centres in the occupied West Bank, harming the prospects for a viable independent Palestinian state, Britain says. “Illegal settlement expansion in the West Bank is destroying the prospects of a two-state solution, so today we are sanctioning companies involved in this activity and disrupting their access to the finance that enables it,” Miliband said in a video posted on X. “And our warning to companies thinking about being part of settlement expansion, including the unconscionable E1 project, is clear: We will clamp down on you.” Britain has long been one of Israel's staunchest allies. Miliband recently described himself as a “proud British Jew” whose grandmother survived the Holocaust. But the U.K. government has grown increasingly critical of Israel's government as the war in Gaza has drawn tens of thousands of protesters onto the streets of London and other cities. Earlier this year, Britain joined five other Western countries in imposing additional sanctions on settlers and settlements. The latest measures target eight property development and construction firms, as well as Tzav 9, an Israeli activist movement that has blocked humanitarian aid convoys from entering Gaza, the government said. The companies are Har Hevron Development Co., Hemdat Shomron, S.A.G. (Velvel) Construction and Development, Lev HaHar Yazamut, Harey Zahav, Ariel Residential Judea & Samaria, Ami Gvirtzman Architects 2021 and Z.F. Building Co. All eight companies and Tzav 9 are now subject to UK asset freezes, and people associated with them will be barred from serving as directors of UK-based companies.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Announcing Britain's plans Sept. 8, Miliband said Israel had crossed a “long-standing red line” by advancing the E1 project. First proposed in the 1990s, it has been repeatedly delayed by international opposition. Israel's outgoing government, dominated by settler leaders, has begun seeking bids to build several thousand homes.

articles.summary: 1. Core Context & Background: The long-discussed E1 project would effectively cut off eastern Jerusalem from Palestinian population centres in the occupied West Bank, harming the prospects for a viable independent Palestinian state, Britain says
articles.keyPoints:
• 1. Core Context & Background: The long-discussed E1 project would effectively cut off eastern Jerusalem from Palestinian population centres in the occupied West Bank, harming the prospects for a viable independent Palestinian state, Britain says
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The UK has sanctioned Israeli construction and property development companies it says are involved in building West Bank settlements, the first concrete step in Britain's previously announced effort to slow the expansion of settlements and preserve the possibility of a two-state solution to the Israeli-Palestinian conflict. The sanctions are the first announced since Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said Sept. 8 that Britain would toughen its stance toward its longtime ally. His announcement followed Israel's decision to seek bids to build 1,200 homes in the E1 area east of Jerusalem and an increase in settler attacks on Palestinians in the West Bank. The long-discussed E1 project would effectively cut off eastern Jerusalem from Palestinian population centres in the occupied West Bank, harming the prospects for a viable independent Palestinian state, Britain says. “Illegal settlement expansion in the West Bank is destroying the prospects of a two-state solution, so today we are sanctioning companies involved in this activity and disrupting their access to the finance that enables it,” Miliband said in a video posted on X. “And our warning to companies thinking about being part of settlement expansion, including the unconscionable E1 project, is clear: We will clamp down on you.” Britain has long been one of Israel's staunchest allies. Miliband recently described himself as a “proud British Jew” whose grandmother survived the Holocaust. But the U.K. government has grown increasingly critical of Israel's government as the war in Gaza has drawn tens of thousands of protesters onto the streets of London and other cities. Earlier this year, Britain joined five other Western countries in imposing additional sanctions on settlers and settlements. The latest measures target eight property development and construction firms, as well as Tzav 9, an Israeli activist movement that has blocked humanitarian aid convoys from entering Gaza, the government said. The companies are Har Hevron Development Co., Hemdat Shomron, S.A.G. (Velvel) Construction and Development, Lev HaHar Yazamut, Harey Zahav, Ariel Residential Judea & Samaria, Ami Gvirtzman Architects 2021 and Z.F. Building Co. All eight companies and Tzav 9 are now subject to UK asset freezes, and people associated with them will be barred from serving as directors of UK-based companies.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Announcing Britain's plans Sept. 8, Miliband said Israel had crossed a “long-standing red line” by advancing the E1 project. First proposed in the 1990s, it has been repeatedly delayed by international opposition. Israel's outgoing government, dominated by settler leaders, has begun seeking bids to build several thousand homes.

articles.title: NATO allies to discuss U.S. troop levels with Pentagon strategy chief
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth unveiled the six-month review in June and threatened to withhold some ‌U.S. dues to NATO if “free riding” allies fell short of defence spending commitments

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: NATO allies will discuss Washington’s review of U.S. troop levels in ​Europe with Pentagon policy chief Elbridge Colby on Tuesday (November 17, 2026), German Defence ⁠Minister Boris Pistorius said, with more clarity on the scope of any drawdown expected within weeks. U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth unveiled the six-month review in June and threatened to withhold some ‌U.S. dues to NATO if “free riding” allies fell short of defence spending commitments. He did not explicitly say the review could lead to cuts ‌in the 80,000 U.S. troops deployed to Europe, but stressed the goal of ‌prompting ⁠the continent to do more while enabling the U.S. military to ⁠meet global commitments. “We expect changes in troop levels, but we don’t know anything concrete yet,” Mr. Pistorius said ahead of a meeting with his EU counterparts in Brussels that Colby will join for a working ​lunch. “But again, a shift in ‌the balance of conventional forces would have occurred under any other U.S. President, due to increased engagement in the Indo-Pacific.” Germany hosts about 35,000 U.S. troops, the largest American military presence in Europe. The result of the review is expected ‌to be presented before Christmas. European military sources have speculated Washington might move ​a brigade or some 5,000 troops from Germany either to Asia or closer to NATO’s eastern flank in Poland. Mr. Pistorius said the ⁠current talks aimed for coordination with Washington to prevent dangerous gaps in NATO’s European defences caused by any U.S. drawdown. Later Mr. Colby ‌will join a meeting of the so-called Ramstein Group of Ukraine’s military supporters at NATO headquarters to discuss how to supply more arms to Kyiv ahead of a harsh winter, while Russia steps up air strikes on civilian infrastructure.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Mr. Pistorius said Germany and Norway would sponsor another package of US weapons under the PURL programme, focusing on supplying more PAC-2 and PAC-3 missiles for the Patriot air defence ‌system to Ukraine.

📰 NATO allies to discuss U.S. troop levels with Pentagon strategy chief

📌 Published: 17 Nov 2026, 11:33:29 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth unveiled the six-month review in June and threatened to withhold some ‌U.S. dues to NATO if “free riding” allies fell short of defence spending commitments

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: NATO allies will discuss Washington’s review of U.S. troop levels in ​Europe with Pentagon policy chief Elbridge Colby on Tuesday (November 17, 2026), German Defence ⁠Minister Boris Pistorius said, with more clarity on the scope of any drawdown expected within weeks. U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth unveiled the six-month review in June and threatened to withhold some ‌U.S. dues to NATO if “free riding” allies fell short of defence spending commitments. He did not explicitly say the review could lead to cuts ‌in the 80,000 U.S. troops deployed to Europe, but stressed the goal of ‌prompting ⁠the continent to do more while enabling the U.S. military to ⁠meet global commitments. “We expect changes in troop levels, but we don’t know anything concrete yet,” Mr. Pistorius said ahead of a meeting with his EU counterparts in Brussels that Colby will join for a working ​lunch. “But again, a shift in ‌the balance of conventional forces would have occurred under any other U.S. President, due to increased engagement in the Indo-Pacific.” Germany hosts about 35,000 U.S. troops, the largest American military presence in Europe. The result of the review is expected ‌to be presented before Christmas. European military sources have speculated Washington might move ​a brigade or some 5,000 troops from Germany either to Asia or closer to NATO’s eastern flank in Poland. Mr. Pistorius said the ⁠current talks aimed for coordination with Washington to prevent dangerous gaps in NATO’s European defences caused by any U.S. drawdown. Later Mr. Colby ‌will join a meeting of the so-called Ramstein Group of Ukraine’s military supporters at NATO headquarters to discuss how to supply more arms to Kyiv ahead of a harsh winter, while Russia steps up air strikes on civilian infrastructure.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Mr. Pistorius said Germany and Norway would sponsor another package of US weapons under the PURL programme, focusing on supplying more PAC-2 and PAC-3 missiles for the Patriot air defence ‌system to Ukraine.

articles.title: Nabeel Rajab, prominent Bahraini human rights activist, dies at 62
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Nabeel Rajab, a prominent democracy activist in Bahrain who helped lead the island nation's 2011 protests known across the wider region as the Arab Spring and who spent years in prison for challenging its monarchy, died on Tuesday (November 17, 2026). He was 62.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: His family found him unresponsive at their home in Turkey on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) morning, activists said. The Bahrain Center for Human Rights, which Rajab once led as president, confirmed his death in a post on X. "We extend our sincere condolences and heartfelt sympathy to his esteemed family. We pray that God may encompass him with his vast mercy and reward him abundantly for his efforts and contributions," the group wrote. Ebrahim Sharif, an activist who was a close friend of the family, said Rajab's wife and daughter found him unresponsive early in the morning at their home in Turkey. He said he had spoken to Rajab's brother and that the family believed Rajab likely died of a heart attack. Rajab left Bahrain early in the Iran war, as authorities cracked down on Shia-led protests throughout the Gulf island kingdom, home to the U.S. Navy's Fifth Fleet. Rajab accused the government of torturing an imprisoned activist and feared he would be arrested if he returned, he told The Associated Press at the time. Rajab rose to international prominence in 2011, as the Arab Spring uprising swept the region and demonstrations erupted in Bahrain's capital, Manama. He was a pivotal figure in the protest movement, during which the country's majority Shiite population demanded the ruling Sunni monarchy offer them greater political freedoms. As president of the Bahrain Centre for Human Rights, he advocated for expanding the powers of Bahrain's parliament, ensuring freedom of expression and fighting anti-Shia discrimination. Bahraini authorities, backed by Saudi troops, arrested scores of demonstrators and crushed the protests, while ultimately introducing limited political reforms. He was imprisoned on multiple occasions in the years following the unrest. His longest stretch behind bars began in June 2016. He was eventually released in June of 2020 during the coronavirus pandemic, though he was ordered to spend the remaining time in home detention.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Rajab had a history of heart issues. During one of his earlier detentions, he received treatment for an irregular heartbeat. He separately received a pardon from King Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa in 2015, after concerns emerged about Rajab's health.

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #24 of 30 (17 NOV)

📰 Nabeel Rajab, prominent Bahraini human rights activist, dies at 62

📌 Published: 17 Nov 2026, 11:27:24 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Nabeel Rajab, a prominent democracy activist in Bahrain who helped lead the island nation's 2011 protests known across the wider region as the Arab Spring and who spent years in prison for challenging its monarchy, died on Tuesday (November 17, 2026). He was 62.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: His family found him unresponsive at their home in Turkey on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) morning, activists said. The Bahrain Center for Human Rights, which Rajab once led as president, confirmed his death in a post on X. "We extend our sincere condolences and heartfelt sympathy to his esteemed family. We pray that God may encompass him with his vast mercy and reward him abundantly for his efforts and contributions," the group wrote. Ebrahim Sharif, an activist who was a close friend of the family, said Rajab's wife and daughter found him unresponsive early in the morning at their home in Turkey. He said he had spoken to Rajab's brother and that the family believed Rajab likely died of a heart attack. Rajab left Bahrain early in the Iran war, as authorities cracked down on Shia-led protests throughout the Gulf island kingdom, home to the U.S. Navy's Fifth Fleet. Rajab accused the government of torturing an imprisoned activist and feared he would be arrested if he returned, he told The Associated Press at the time. Rajab rose to international prominence in 2011, as the Arab Spring uprising swept the region and demonstrations erupted in Bahrain's capital, Manama. He was a pivotal figure in the protest movement, during which the country's majority Shiite population demanded the ruling Sunni monarchy offer them greater political freedoms. As president of the Bahrain Centre for Human Rights, he advocated for expanding the powers of Bahrain's parliament, ensuring freedom of expression and fighting anti-Shia discrimination. Bahraini authorities, backed by Saudi troops, arrested scores of demonstrators and crushed the protests, while ultimately introducing limited political reforms. He was imprisoned on multiple occasions in the years following the unrest. His longest stretch behind bars began in June 2016. He was eventually released in June of 2020 during the coronavirus pandemic, though he was ordered to spend the remaining time in home detention.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Rajab had a history of heart issues. During one of his earlier detentions, he received treatment for an irregular heartbeat. He separately received a pardon from King Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa in 2015, after concerns emerged about Rajab's health.

अनुत्तरदायी — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Unresponsive' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।

महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Prominence' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।

Rajab accused the government of torturing an imprisoned activist and feared he would be arrested if he returned, he told The Associated Press at the time. Rajab rose to international prominence in 2011, as the Arab Spring uprising swept the region and demonstrations erupted in Bahrain's capital, Manama. He was a pivotal figure in the protest movement, during which the country's majority Shiite population demanded the ruling Sunni monarchy offer them greater political freedoms. As president of the Bahrain Centre for Human Rights, he advocated for expanding the powers of Bahrain's parliament, ensuring freedom of expression and fighting anti-Shia discrimination. Bahraini authorities, backed by Saudi troops, arrested scores of demonstrators and crushed the protests, while ultimately introducing limited political reforms. He was imprisoned on multiple occasions in the years following the unrest. His longest stretch behind bars began in June 2016. He was eventually released in June of 2020 during the coronavirus pandemic, though he was ordered to spend the remaining time in home detention.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Rajab had a history of heart issues. During one of his earlier detentions, he received treatment for an irregular heartbeat. He separately received a pardon from King Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa in 2015, after concerns emerged about Rajab's health.

hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — जबकि एआई और मशीन लर्निंग भारत के आधिकारिक आंकड़ों को तेज़ और व्यापक बनाने का वादा करते हैं, वे स्वचालित रूप से जमीनी स्तर के साक्ष्य को प्रतिस्थापित नहीं कर सकते हैं; विरासत में मिली सीमाओं के साथ सिंथेटिक डेटा से सार्वजनिक संसाधनों का गलत आवंटन और आर्थिक संकेतकों में विकृति आ सकती है। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Comprehensive' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Comprehensive' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive और Antonyms हैं: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile।

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: India must shore up its partnerships in the Asian region

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Each year, the summits of the 11-member Association of South-East Asian Nations mark an important moment on the diplomatic calendar: India is able to interact with all of its partners in the Indo-Pacific and engage global powers at the ASEAN-India Summit and the East Asia Summit. Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s talks with Indo-Pacific players focused on a future shaped “not by competition, but by cooperation”. This year, the summit in Manila hosted by the Philippines had many other imperatives. These were the first ASEAN summits since the U.S.-Israel attacks on Iran and Iran’s Hormuz blockade and strikes on Gulf countries that have upended energy and trade across South and South East Asia. Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s call for “peace, stability, and predictability” in the world during the EAS was aimed as much at leaders from the U.S., Russia and China as it was for the region. The visit had a bilateral context — the Philippines and India have intensified ties considerably in the past year, since the visit of President Bongbong Marcos to Delhi in August 2025, including the upgradation of the Strategic Partnership, maritime exchanges and negotiations over the supply of more Indian-made Brahmos missile battery systems to the Philippines. This year, after months of concerns about U.S. President Donald Trump’s lack of interest in the Quad grouping, the U.S. decided to host a summit of U.S.-India-Australia-Japan Quad leaders on the side-lines of the ASEAN summits, the first time the summit has been held in a non-Quad country.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Given the stakes, there were several outcomes from all the three summits that PM Modi attended back-to-back on Tuesday — the ASEAN India Summit launched a new cooperation on disaster management, and the East Asia Summit focused on countering cyber-crime. PM Modi’s announcement that India would give all ASEAN citizens free tourist visas is expected to increase people-to-people interactions and trade. At the Quad summit, President Trump made a number of announcements including the launch of a Quad Business leaders forum, to be held in Mumbai next year, and the first Quad naval exercises with patrol aircraft. However, the outcomes in Manila paled in significance to the anticipation over Mr. Trump’s next stop in Shenzhen for the Asia Pacific Economic Conference (APEC), with an unprecedented three-way summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping planned on Thursday. New Delhi must watch the outcomes of that summit among the “global superpowers” much more closely.

On November 11, a terror attack on a checkpoint manned by the personnel of the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) in Kulgam left three jawans injured. On November 16, a local, whom the police suspected of having joined the terror ranks a few days ago, was killed after six days of a siege-like anti-terror operation in residential areas of Kulgam. In Jammu’s Kishtwar, two Special Police Officers (SPOs) of the J&K Police were found dead with bullet wounds, a day after they were reported missing in a forest range on November 11. The anti-terror operation in civilian areas of Kulgam has raised concerns. Former J&K Chief Minister and PDP president Mehbooba Mufti described the operation, spread over six days, as “collective punishment that only breeds alienation and resentment,” while NC spokesman Imran Nabi Dar suggested that entire villages were put under prolonged restrictions for days. The Omar Abdullah government , because of limited powers and no jurisdiction over the police in J&K, a Union Territory since 2019, finds itself hamstrung. The iron hand policy to stamp out terrorism and separatism has been effective from a strictly security perspective — terror attacks as well as local recruitments into terror ranks have declined. According to the police, local recruits have come down to single digit or fewer than 10 in Kashmir.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: That said, the decline in terrorist incidents and the silence of the streets should not be mistaken for peace. The current situation demands a political reach-out by the Centre to all the stakeholders of J&K. It has to begin with the much-promised restoration of Statehood , which will give the voters a sense that their mass participation in the 2024 Assembly elections allowed their elected leaders to hold institutions accountable, and they were able to work freely to protect the interests of the region. Though the security agencies need to be focused on Pakistan-backed terrorism, it should not come at the cost of re-inflicting psychological scars within Kashmir, which could turn into a powder keg if left unattended. Healing through both political and security processes has to be complementary rather than conflicting. Allowing the political class of J&K to establish its writ and providing room to security agencies to combat challenges are not contradictory.

1. Core Context & Background: Death penalty requires a near-infallible criminal justice system

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: India’s vote against a proposed global moratorium on the death penalty at the UN is consistent with its position at the forum; it has defended its retention of the penalty as a sovereign decision backed by judicial safeguards, including the “rarest of rare” condition and sessions courts’ sentences requiring a High Court’s confirmation. At the same time, the Supreme Court has increasingly restricted capital punishment and research has failed to find evidence of additional deterrence over life imprisonment . India’s distinction between judicial executions and extrajudicial killings is legally valid but its further claim that due process protects people facing execution is less so. While India last executed convicts in 2020, for the Delhi gang-rape and murder, Parliament expanded the number of capital offences under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita — a form of penal populism that projects the political attractiveness of the state’s response to public outrage, especially in cases of sexual violence, without addressing the poor policing and low conviction rates that actually undermine deterrence . The country had 574 people on death row on December 31, 2025, the highest since 2016, thanks to trial court rulings, challenging claims about judicial safeguards in practice. The report of the 2015 Law Commission headed by Justice A.P. Shah said the death penalty “fails to achieve any constitutionally valid penological goals” and recommended abolishing it for all crimes except terrorism and waging war. Only a small group of countries worldwide are executing more people. In India, per Project 39A, the Supreme Court released 38 persons from death row in 2016-2025 after they had spent eight years there on average. Some have endured more than two decades. The punishment requires a measure of infallibility that the criminal justice system cannot supply. The safeguards neither deter convictions in cases with flawed evidence, false testimony, and so on nor remedy unequal access to competent legal representation among those facing the penalty. India should formally suspend executions and commission a review of penalty statutes and the treatment of prisoners on death row. Second, it should spare offences that do not involve intentional killing from the penalty. Research suggests meting out excessively harsh punishments for non-fatal crimes could incentivise offenders to escalate their violence, including to kill potential witnesses. The greater goal should be to abolish the practice in law while improving investigative and prosecutorial practices and access to legal aid.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: prison / judiciary (system of justice) / crime, law and justice / United Nations / death penalty policies

1. Core Context & Background: The dangers of centralising the internet’s architecture are now clear

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Last week, Microsoft’s suite of productivity and email software, which businesses, governments, hospitals and a host of other organisations rely upon round-the-clock, abruptly stopped working globally , affecting tens of millions of people around the world. The company has cited a network upgrade gone awry as the root cause of the incident. Incidents such as the Microsoft 365 outage are a natural consequence of businesses and governments allowing key digital systems to become centralised all over the world. The internet remains, and was pioneered as, a network of networks. If one business’s networks went down, the reasoning went, others would not fall like dominos: everyone was, after all, connected to everyone else. But the economics have long been prohibitive, with dedicated servers and web-connected infrastructure infeasible for all but the largest businesses, with even those firms seeking the enticing cost savings from socialised infrastructure. That made sense: the internet made shared infrastructure more economical, allowing hardware and maintenance costs to be spread so far and wide that at a per-user level prices have been negligible. Competition among major cloud providers, the few that remain at Microsoft’s scale, have kept prices affordable for enterprise software for all shades of organisations.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Digital services have grown more sophisticated, and more deeply integrated into the economy as this centralisation unfolded. But the downside is that, regardless of the sophistication and professionalism of any company, mistakes happen, and the scale of these mistakes can quickly cascade over to the entire economy. There are societal and organisational lessons to be gleaned from these episodes. There is no such thing as a reliable vendor. Governments must also draw a cyber sovereignty lesson here that does not simply entail swapping a global vendor for a domestic one. It is the subversion of the internet’s architecture that is at the root of these incidents. Investing in resilience — and shielding critical operations from destabilising disruptions, no matter how improbable — should inform attitudes to digital systems. As a new generation of AI data centres is poised to supercharge the centralised systems of yesteryear, it is all the more imperative to mitigate even occasional vagaries of large systems.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: While maintaining its hard stance on cross-border terrorism, India has an opportunity to recognise that many of its other interests still merit sustained cooperation with Pakistan as the latter’s climate minister Musadik Masood Malik prepares to attend the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue Forum in New Delhi. India’s official position since the Pahalgam attack and the ensuing confrontations along the border is that terrorism and bilateral talks cannot coexist. A month later, Prime Minister Narendra Modi signalled that India’s relations with Pakistan would remain subordinate to its demands on cross-border terrorism by extending the condition to trade and water. South Asia is already one of the least economically integrated regions worldwide, with intra-regional trade at around 5%, and, as Chatham House has inferred, strained ties between India and its neighbours have created diplomatic vacuums that Beijing has taken advantage of through trilateral and regional groupings. Now, by inviting all SCO members to the national capital and participating in meetings ahead of the August 2027 Islamabad Summit, New Delhi has shown some maturity as a convening power. Islamabad is also being pragmatic in keeping channels open during its SCO chairmanship by participating in an initiative championed by Mr. Modi.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The pursuit of regionwide water security remains particularly fluid, with India seemingly overlooking the fact that it is upstream of Pakistan and Bangladesh and downstream of China. After India stopped sharing routine hydrological data of the Indus river and approved the Chenab-Beas link tunnel project, Mr. Malik fanned the flames saying Pakistan would “cut off those hands” seeking to restrict its share of the water. Yet China has now restricted the same data vis-à-vis the Brahmaputra while it builds the Medog mega-dam in Tibet. India has also protested the proposed Padma Barrage in Bangladesh, which has been increasing its alignment with China, echoing India building the Farakka Barrage over East Pakistan’s objections in 1961. Climate change is rendering cooperation more essential to manage the integrity of contested geographies, the willingness of border populations to engage, and the potential to generate hydroelectric power. New Delhi should retreat from the notion that working together on the Indus will be a concession to Islamabad and see in the Dialogue an opportunity to restore the necessary channels. Suspending ties may communicate political resolve but will not diminish terrorists’ capabilities in the region or improve India’s security. It has already compromised India’s ambitions to regional leadership, which require the ability to keep engaging even with difficult neighbours. India should go beyond using multilateral fora to assert its national position and start identifying areas where bilateral cooperation serves its interests, including with Pakistan.

Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Islam is projected to be the world's largest religion by 2035, surpassing Christianity, according to a new study released by the Pew Research Centre on Wednesday (November 18, 2026). Pew said if current trends continue, there will be more than 3.6 billion Muslims and just under three billion Christians worldwide by 2070. The absolute number of Hindus in India and worldwide will rise from 1.2 billion in 2020 to 1.4 billion by 2070. But the rest of the world's population -- all non-Hindus -- will grow at an even faster rate. As a result, Hindus will shrink slightly as a share of the global population, falling from 15% in 2020 to 14% in 2070. The world's total population is projected to increase by 29% between 2020 and 2070, with Christians growing by 30% and Muslims by 80%. "The largest source of new members of major religions is not adults who convert to the faith, but babies who are born into the group," the Pew projections found. During 2020-2025, the fertility rate for Muslims was 3.1 children per woman, followed by the rate for Christians at 2.5, Pew said. The average fertility rate for all other women was 1.6, below the 2.1 level considered necessary for each generation to replace itself. If current demographic trends continue, the number of Hindus in India will increase by 176 million between 2020 and 2070. While India's overall fertility rate has fallen rapidly in recent decades, Muslims in India still have more children per woman than Hindus do, the Pew Research found. As per the Pew projections, Hindus comprise 79.4% of India's religious composition in 2020 and the number is set to slide to 75.8% by 2070. Muslims comprise 15.2% of India's religious composition in 2020, and that share is set to rise to 19.6% by 2070. Outside India, much of the projected growth among Hindus will come from Pakistan (over five million) and the United States (over four million).

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: According to the Pew projections, the U.S. will have the world's fifth-largest Hindu population. Nepal and India will remain the only two countries with a Hindu majority.

Each public tap costs the Corporation ₹21,838 a year, irrespective of whether it is functional, taking the total annual expenditure to ₹11.70 crore. Until the previous government completely wrote off the water charge arrears, around ₹5 crore used to be deducted annually from the Corporation’s Plan fund towards the dues. Mayor V.K. Minimol said that despite free water connections provided under the Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation, several divisions still had more than 50 and even 100 public taps. The 18 divisions in West Kochi alone accounted for 2,216 taps, of which 1,623 were non-functional, translating into an annual expenditure of over ₹3.54 crore. Earavely division has the highest number of taps (263), followed by Mattancherry (215), Kalvathy (189), and Karippalam (174). “Councillors should take a serious look at this list and scrutinise it further so that only those taps that are absolutely necessary are retained and the rest surrendered to the KWA. To check misuse of public taps, they will be remodelled with concrete structures, as was done in the past, and fitted with meters,” Ms. Minimol said. LDF parliamentary party leader V.A. Sreejith said that while taps that are no longer in use could be surrendered, councillors should not be made responsible for issuing letters to the KWA seeking their removal. This, he said, would spare councillors from having to bear the brunt of public resentment over such a move.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: BJP councillor Priya Prasanth said it was imperative to ensure the availability of drinking water in an area before scrapping an existing public tap. Despite having water connections, there could still be households without a reliable water supply and, therefore, dependent on public taps. Such taps should be retained, she added.

Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: With traffic congestion worsening as the city expands, Hyderabad is exploring a 35-km Personal Rapid Transit System (PRTS) to improve connectivity along key corridors. The proposal is under active consideration, with the first phase envisaged between Kukatpally and Knowledge City via Raidurgam and Biodiversity Park. The proposed stretch would have 64 stations. Officials made a presentation on the plan to Chief Secretary Sanjay Jaju at a meeting here on Wednesday. The presentation followed directions from the Chief Secretary to prepare an action plan after Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy suggested exploring PRTS as an alternative mode of transport to ease congestion along important corridors. Mr. Jaju called for a comprehensive strategy to address the growing traffic challenges arising from the city’s rapid expansion. Hyderabad Metro Rail officials, who studied the feasibility of PRTS and other transport systems, projected daily commuter demand at 3.94 lakh by 2030, 7.96 lakh by 2040 and 10 lakh by 2050. Mr. Jaju asked officials to identify potential PRTS corridors based on traffic density and ensure optimum use of existing transport systems. He also stressed that the proposed network should be developed at minimum cost. Hyderabad Metro Rail Limited officials were directed to expedite consultations with technical experts and potential project partners.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: He also called for effective coordination among departments, including Municipal Administration, Energy, South Central Railway and HYDRAA, to ensure integrated traffic planning that takes the city’s future needs into account.

1. Core Context & Background: This comes days after The Hindu reported that at least 287 entries such as ISKCON, Gorak Nath, Sanatan, Vedic Dharm, Ramdev etc. had been listed in a drop-down menu for “Other” religions on the portal and then removed

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The 2027 Census self-enumeration portal is now showing a total of 76 entries under the “Other” religions that now appear as predictive text suggestions and not as a drop-down menu. This comes days after The Hindu reported that at least 287 entries such as ISKCON, Ramkrishna Paramhans, Gorak Nath , Sanatan, Vedic Dharm, Ramdev etc., had been listed in a drop-down menu for “Other” religions on the portal and then removed. An examination of the new list of available “Other” religions showed that the Union government removed over 200 entries that were previously listed under the same category on Monday (November 16, 2026), the day the portal went live for four poll-bound States — Uttar Pradesh, Goa, Punjab and Uttarakhand. The deletions include entries such as Satguru, Ramdev, ISKCON, Ramkrishna Paramhans, Gorak Nath, Sanatan, Bishnoi, Vaishnaw, Shia, Sunni, and many others that were either classified in earlier Censuses as sects within the six major religions (Hindu, Muslim, Christian, Sikh, Jain, Buddhist) or seemed to be new entries not recorded in previous Censuses at all. Out of the 76 predictive text suggestions that now remain on the portal, nearly all appear to have already been recorded and tabulated based on the 2011 Census data on what people chose to write their faith as under the “Other” column. A majority of these entries include the religions and faiths of Scheduled Tribe communities across the country — such as Sarna, Doni Polo, Tana Bhagat, Birsa, Garo, Munda, Oraon, Santal, etc. Apart from these, five entries in this new list of suggestive “other” religions do not feature in the 2011 or 2001 Census tables for “Other religions and persuasions”. These include “Adibasi dharma”, “Bura Deo”, “Karupa”, “Tingkao Rangong”, and “Tingwang Hingde”. Soon after The Hindu reported the presence of a drop-down for “other” religions and its quick removal, Opposition leaders and OBC associations alike questioned the integrity of the way the 2027 Census was being conducted, with many of them questioning how the government was comfortable introducing a drop-down for religions but not for caste. Experts had also questioned the introduction of previously unrecorded entries in this drop-down, saying there would be nothing to compare these with. Interestingly, a section of general category communities in north India reacted to the presence of 287 “other” religions by saying this was an alleged attempt to “divide Hindus”. On Monday (November 16, 2026), when the self-enumeration portal went live, the initial list of 287 entries for “Other” religions appeared as a drop-down menu from which respondents could select one in addition to writing in whatever they wanted. Within hours of The Hindu sending a query to the Union Home Ministry, this drop-down menu was removed, and a representative of the Office of the RGI and the Census Commissioner said it would be “incorrect” to say these entries were shown as “other” religions.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: However, a government official had told The Hindu at the time that this list was part of “predictive text entries” to help reduce variations and mistakes in spellings. But officials did not clarify how previously unrecorded entries such as ISKCON, Ramkrishna Paramhans, Ramdev, Gorak Nath, etc. had appeared on this list either.
